environment.description: Same service binary deployed in a hardened container on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (grpc_proxy_t). The TE policy uses a narrow file context specification: allow grpc_proxy_t grpc_proxy_conf_t:file { read open getattr }; with only /opt/service/config(/.*)? labeled grpc_proxy_conf_t. All other file types have no allow rule for grpc_proxy_t. The policy also restricts grpc_proxy_t to only connect to port 50051 (corenet_tcp_connect_grpc_port). Additionally, the container runtime applies a seccomp profile that blocks execve for any binary not matching /usr/local/bin/grpcurl (via a BPF argument filter on the pathname). The combination means: (1) path traversal reads are denied by SELinux even if the path resolves correctly because the target file won't have grpc_proxy_conf_t label, and (2) the grpcurl command injection cannot pivot to arbitrary command execution due to seccomp restrictions.

selinux_te_rules: allow grpc_proxy_t grpc_proxy_conf_t:file { read open getattr };
config.seccomp_profile: custom-grpcproxy.json with execve filtered to allow only /usr/local/bin/grpcurl via SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW on arg0 match
